texts.facts: The petitioner is a resident of Thiruvananthapuram and is a person with locomotor disability. The permanent disability is assessed at 40%. The petitioner started a small food truck restaurant business near Chackai in Thiruvananthapuram. Along with this food truck, he also obtained a small shop in the vicinity for the production, catering and sale of food products. The food truck motor vehicle is also having requisite license and registration to be used as a mobile canteen. 2. The petitioner states that the petitioner has been running and operating this food truck and restaurant in full compliance of all Rules and Regulations, Food Safety Standards and maintaining absolute law and order in the area. 2025 : KER:55847 The 4th respondent set up an unauthorized shack in close proximity to the food truck and shop of the petitioner a few months after the petitioner started operating his restaurant. Respondents 5 and 6 are the children of the 4 th respondent. From the time, respondents 4 to 6 set up their unauthorized shack (Thattukada) and started functioning as an illegal restaurant, they have been creating grave law and order situation, endangering the life, property, and business of the petitioner and his family. On numerous occasions they have created environment of high criminal intimidation. 3. The petitioner further submits that in a bid to purposely create nuisance and bodily injury to the petitioner and his family, respondents 4 to 6 on numerous occasions have trespassed into the restaurant and shop of the petitioner, assaulted the petitioner, his wife and 10 year old daughter and have physically assaulted and abused the minor child of the petitioner. Despite Exts.P7 to P10 complaints, respondents 4 2025:KER:55847 to 6 with the aid of other anti social elements and goondas would surround the food truck of the petitioner shout at the petitioner and his family hurl obscene abuses and threaten them and their restaurant patrons with bodily injury if they do not stop their operations. 4. To the shock of the petitioner, the 3 rd respondent threatened the petitioner and stated that he will charge cases against the petitioner and make his life unlivable if he does not immediately close down his shop. He further directed the petitioner to immediately stop all business and close his restaurant failing which he threatened to arrest the petitioner and his family members in false cases. Thinking about the welfare of the family of the petitioner and intimidated by the threats of this senior police officer, the petitioner on 16.05.2025 closed the food truck restaurant and informed the same to the 3rd respondent. The Standing Counsel submitted that for running a Thattukada, a licence is not necessary, but registration is mandatory. The petitioner has applied for registration as per Ext.P6. 6. 8. The pleadings would indicate that the petitioner is a physically handicapped person with locomotor disability. is the Disability Certificate issued to the petitioner by the Medical Officer, Thiruvananthapuram. By Ext.P3, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India has granted Registration Certificate to the petitioner. Ext.P6 would indicate that the petitioner has also sought for registration under the Kerala Municipalities Act from the Thiruvananthapuram Municipal Corporation. 9. When the petitioner is running the Thattukada after obtaining necessary statutory permissions, if any gathering of criminals, anti-social elements are found near the Thattukada of the petitioner during the night hours, it is the 2025:KER:55847 duty of the police to remove such anti-social criminals. That cannot be a reason to shut down the Thattukada of the petitioner. In the circumstances, the writ petition is disposed of directing the 3rd respondent not to obstruct the petitioner from running Thattukada, as long as the petitioner holds FSSAI licence.
texts.arguments: Therefore, the petitioner is before this Court seeking to direct the police to permit the petitioner 2025:KER:55847 to open and operate his restaurant and to accord police protection to the life, limb, and business of the petitioner and his family. Government Pleader entered appearance and submitted that at the place where the petitioner is running the Thattukada, during the night, a large number of anti-social and criminal elements Arun Arjun vs State Of Kerala on 28 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55660805/ 3 gathering and it was in the interest of public safety that the petitioner was directed not to run the shop during the night hours. The petitioner would submit that the petitioner is not running the Thattukada throughout the night and the petitioner's shop will be closed by around 11 pm.
